```{r analysis, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
install.packages(c("ordinal", "lme4", "lmerTest", "emmeans", "broom.mixed"))
# ============================================================
# 0. SETUP
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(ordinal)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(broom.mixed)

setwd("/work")

# Participant and experiment structure
expected_participants <- 8
trials_per_block <- 60
expected_blocks <- 10

# ============================================================
# 1. IMPORT DATA
# ============================================================

# Locate all participant CSV files
files <- list.files(
  path = "behav",
  pattern = ".*_experiment_data\\.csv",
  full.names = TRUE
)

if (length(files) == 0) {
  stop("No participant CSV files found in /work/behav.")
}

# Read all files and extract participant IDs from filenames
df_raw <- purrr::map_dfr(files, function(file_path) {

  participant_id <- stringr::str_extract(
    basename(file_path),
    "\\d{4}"
  )

  if (is.na(participant_id)) {
    stop(paste("Could not extract participant ID from:", file_path))
  }

  readr::read_csv(
    file_path,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      subject = participant_id,
      source_file = basename(file_path)
    )
})

# Check that the required columns exist
required_columns <- c(
  "subject",
  "target_type",
  "objective_response",
  "subjective_response",
  "objective_response_time_ms",
  "target_contrast"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(df_raw)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste(
      "Missing required columns:",
      paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}

# Check participant count
cat("Number of participants:", n_distinct(df_raw$subject), "\n")
cat("Total number of trials:", nrow(df_raw), "\n")

if (n_distinct(df_raw$subject) != expected_participants) {
  warning("The number of participants differs from the expected 8.")
}

```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# 2. CLEAN AND PREPARE DATA
# ============================================================

df_clean <- df_raw %>%

  # Clean text columns
  mutate(
    subject = factor(subject),

    target_type = stringr::str_trim(
      as.character(target_type)
    ),

    objective_response = stringr::str_trim(
      as.character(objective_response)
    ),

    # Convert behavioural variables to numeric
    subjective_response = as.numeric(subjective_response),

    objective_response_time_ms = as.numeric(
      objective_response_time_ms
    ),

    target_contrast = as.numeric(target_contrast)
  ) %>%

  # Remove trials without a valid target orientation
  filter(
    target_type %in% c("stimulus_0", "stimulus_1")
  ) %>%

  # Translate stimulus labels into target orientations
  mutate(
    orientation_label = case_when(
      target_type == "stimulus_0" ~ "45° (Right)",
      target_type == "stimulus_1" ~ "135° (Left)"
    ),

    orientation_label = factor(
      orientation_label,
      levels = c("45° (Right)", "135° (Left)")
    ),

    # Correctness: whether the objective response matches
    # the presented target stimulus
    is_correct = as.integer(
      objective_response == target_type
    ),

    # PAS response as an ordered categorical variable
    pas_ord = ordered(
      subjective_response,
      levels = 1:4
    )
  ) %>%

  # Reconstruct experimental blocks using trial order
  # Each participant completed 600 trials:
  # 60 trials per block, resulting in 10 blocks.
  group_by(subject) %>%

  mutate(
    trial_in_subject = row_number(),

    block = ((trial_in_subject - 1) %/% trials_per_block) + 1,

    block = factor(
      block,
      levels = 1:expected_blocks
    )
  ) %>%

  ungroup() %>%

  # Remove trials with invalid PAS values
  # PAS must be between 1 and 4.
  mutate(
    pas_ord = ordered(
      subjective_response,
      levels = 1:4
    )
  )

# Check block reconstruction
block_check <- df_clean %>%
  count(subject, block)

print(block_check)

# Check orientation distribution
print(
  df_clean %>%
    count(orientation_label)
)

# Check missingness in important variables
missingness <- df_clean %>%
  summarise(
    missing_orientation = sum(is.na(orientation_label)),
    missing_accuracy = sum(is.na(is_correct)),
    missing_PAS = sum(is.na(pas_ord)),
    missing_RT = sum(is.na(objective_response_time_ms)),
    missing_contrast = sum(is.na(target_contrast))
  )

print(missingness)

```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# 3. DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS
# ============================================================

# Overall descriptive statistics by orientation
descriptive_summary <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(orientation_label) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),

    accuracy = mean(is_correct, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_PAS = mean(
      subjective_response,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    mean_RT = mean(
      objective_response_time_ms,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    sd_RT = sd(
      objective_response_time_ms,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(descriptive_summary)

# Descriptive statistics by orientation and block
block_summary <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(orientation_label, block) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),

    accuracy = mean(is_correct, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_PAS = mean(
      subjective_response,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    mean_RT = mean(
      objective_response_time_ms,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(block_summary)
```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# 4. H1: SUBJECTIVE PERCEPTUAL CLARITY (PAS)
# ============================================================

# H1:
# PAS ratings are comparable between the two target
# orientations after accounting for experimental block.
#
# PAS is ordinal (1-4), so a cumulative link mixed model
# is used instead of treating PAS as a continuous variable.
#
# Subject is included as a random intercept to account
# for repeated observations from each participant.

df_pas <- df_clean %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(pas_ord),
    !is.na(orientation_label),
    !is.na(block)
  )

pas_model <- ordinal::clmm(
  pas_ord ~ orientation_label + block +
    (1 | subject),

  data = df_pas,
  link = "logit",
  Hess = TRUE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

# Model results
cat("\n---------------- H1: PAS MODEL ----------------\n")
print(summary(pas_model))

# Confidence intervals for model parameters
print(confint(pas_model))

# Estimated PAS category probabilities by orientation
pas_emmeans <- emmeans(
  pas_model,
  ~ orientation_label,
  mode = "prob"
)

cat("\nEstimated PAS probabilities by orientation:\n")
print(pas_emmeans)

# Pairwise orientation comparison on the latent scale
pas_orientation_comparison <- emmeans(
  pas_model,
  pairwise ~ orientation_label,
  mode = "latent"
)

cat("\nPAS orientation comparison:\n")
print(pas_orientation_comparison)

```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# H1 PLOT 1: PAS DISTRIBUTION BY ORIENTATION
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate each participant's proportion of responses
# in each PAS category. Averaging these proportions means
# each participant contributes equally to the group result.

pas_distribution <- df_pas %>%
  group_by(subject, orientation_label, subjective_response) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(subject, orientation_label) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(orientation_label, subjective_response) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_proportion = mean(proportion, na.rm = TRUE),

    se = sd(proportion, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(n_distinct(df_pas$subject)),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    PAS = factor(
      subjective_response,
      levels = 1:4,
      labels = c(
        "1 - No experience",
        "2 - Brief glimpse",
        "3 - Almost clear",
        "4 - Clear"
      )
    )
  )

ggplot(
  pas_distribution,
  aes(
    x = orientation_label,
    y = mean_proportion,
    fill = PAS
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = "stack",
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "PAS Distribution by Target Orientation",
    x = "Target Orientation",
    y = "Proportion of PAS Responses",
    fill = "PAS Rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# H1 PLOT 2: PAS ACROSS EXPERIMENTAL BLOCKS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Mean PAS is used here only for descriptive visualisation.
# The ordinal mixed model above remains the inferential test.

pas_block_subject <- df_pas %>%
  group_by(subject, orientation_label, block) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_PAS = mean(
      subjective_response,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pas_block_summary <- pas_block_subject %>%
  group_by(orientation_label, block) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_PAS = mean(mean_PAS, na.rm = TRUE),

    se = sd(mean_PAS, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(n()),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  pas_block_summary,
  aes(
    x = block,
    y = mean_PAS,
    colour = orientation_label,
    group = orientation_label
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_PAS - se,
      ymax = mean_PAS + se
    ),
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = 1:4,
    limits = c(1, 4)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Perceptual Clarity Across Experimental Blocks",
    x = "Experimental Block",
    y = "Mean PAS Rating",
    colour = "Target Orientation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 5. H2: ORIENTATION-DISCRIMINATION ACCURACY
# ============================================================

# H2:
# Accuracy is comparable between the two target orientations
# after accounting for experimental block.
#
# Accuracy is binary (correct/incorrect), so a binomial
# logistic mixed model is used.
#
# Target contrast is included as a control variable because
# stimulus visibility may influence discrimination accuracy.
#
# Subject is included as a random intercept.

df_accuracy <- df_clean %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(is_correct),
    !is.na(orientation_label),
    !is.na(block),
    !is.na(target_contrast)
  )

accuracy_model <- lme4::glmer(
  is_correct ~ orientation_label +
    target_contrast +
    block +
    (1 | subject),

  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  data = df_accuracy,

  control = glmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa",
    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)
  )
)

cat("\n---------------- H2: ACCURACY MODEL ----------------\n")
print(summary(accuracy_model))

# Confidence intervals for model parameters
print(confint(
  accuracy_model,
  parm = "beta_",
  method = "Wald"
))

# Estimated accuracy probabilities by orientation
accuracy_emmeans <- emmeans(
  accuracy_model,
  ~ orientation_label,
  type = "response"
)

cat("\nEstimated accuracy by orientation:\n")
print(accuracy_emmeans)

# Pairwise comparison between orientations
accuracy_comparison <- pairs(
  accuracy_emmeans
)

cat("\nAccuracy orientation comparison:\n")
print(accuracy_comparison)

```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# H2 PLOT 1: ACCURACY ACROSS EXPERIMENTAL BLOCKS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate accuracy for each participant, orientation,
# and block. Group means and standard errors are then
# calculated across participants rather than trials.

accuracy_block_subject <- df_accuracy %>%
  group_by(subject, orientation_label, block) %>%
  summarise(
    accuracy = mean(is_correct, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

accuracy_block_summary <- accuracy_block_subject %>%
  group_by(orientation_label, block) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_accuracy = mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),

    se = sd(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(n()),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  accuracy_block_summary,
  aes(
    x = block,
    y = mean_accuracy,
    colour = orientation_label,
    group = orientation_label
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 6. H2: RESPONSE TIME
# ============================================================

# Response time is analysed only for correct trials.
# Incorrect responses may reflect different decision processes
# and are therefore not included in the primary RT analysis.
#
# RT is usually right-skewed, so it is log-transformed.
# The model estimates differences in log response time.
#
# Target contrast and block are included as fixed effects.
# Subject is included as a random intercept.

df_rt <- df_clean %>%
  filter(
    is_correct == 1,
    !is.na(objective_response_time_ms),
    objective_response_time_ms > 0,
    !is.na(orientation_label),
    !is.na(block),
    !is.na(target_contrast)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log_RT = log(objective_response_time_ms)
  )

rt_model <- lmerTest::lmer(
  log_RT ~ orientation_label +
    target_contrast +
    block +
    (1 | subject),

  data = df_rt,
  REML = FALSE
)

cat("\n---------------- H2: RESPONSE TIME MODEL ----------------\n")
print(summary(rt_model))

# Confidence intervals for model parameters
print(confint(
  rt_model,
  method = "Wald"
))

# Estimated response times by orientation.
# Results are initially on the log scale.
rt_emmeans <- emmeans(
  rt_model,
  ~ orientation_label
)

cat("\nEstimated log response times by orientation:\n")
print(rt_emmeans)

# Pairwise comparison on the log scale
rt_comparison <- pairs(
  rt_emmeans
)

cat("\nResponse time orientation comparison:\n")
print(rt_comparison)

# Exponentiate the orientation difference to obtain
# the response-time ratio between orientations.
#
# A ratio of 1 indicates equal response times.
# A ratio above 1 indicates longer RT for the second
# orientation relative to the first.

cat("\nResponse-time ratio comparison:\n")

rt_comparison_results <- as.data.frame(
  summary(
    rt_comparison,
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
  )
)

print(rt_comparison_results)

# Identify the confidence interval column names
lower_col <- grep(
  "lower.CL|LCL",
  names(rt_comparison_results),
  value = TRUE
)[1]

upper_col <- grep(
  "upper.CL|UCL",
  names(rt_comparison_results),
  value = TRUE
)[1]

# Convert log-scale estimates and confidence intervals
# into response-time ratios
rt_comparison_results <- rt_comparison_results %>%
  mutate(
    RT_ratio = exp(estimate),
    lower_ratio = if (!is.na(lower_col)) {
      exp(.data[[lower_col]])
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    upper_ratio = if (!is.na(upper_col)) {
      exp(.data[[upper_col]])
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  )

print(rt_comparison_results)
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# H2 PLOT 2: RESPONSE TIME ACROSS EXPERIMENTAL BLOCKS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate participant-level mean RT for each
# orientation and block, then calculate group mean and SE.

rt_block_subject <- df_rt %>%
  group_by(subject, orientation_label, block) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_RT = mean(
      objective_response_time_ms,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

rt_block_summary <- rt_block_subject %>%
  group_by(orientation_label, block) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_RT = mean(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE),

    se = sd(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(n()),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  rt_block_summary,
  aes(
    x = block,
    y = mean_RT,
    colour = orientation_label,
    group = orientation_label
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 7. MODEL DIAGNOSTICS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# H1: PAS MODEL
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Check model convergence and warnings
cat("\nH1 convergence information:\n")
print(pas_model$optRes$convergence)

# Check estimated random-effect variance
cat("\nH1 random effects:\n")
print(VarCorr(pas_model))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# H2: ACCURACY MODEL
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Check convergence and singularity
cat("\nH2 accuracy model convergence:\n")
print(accuracy_model@optinfo$conv)

cat("\nH2 accuracy model singularity:\n")
print(isSingular(accuracy_model))

# Basic residual simulation is recommended for a
# binomial GLMM. DHARMa can be used if installed.
if (requireNamespace("DHARMa", quietly = TRUE)) {

  accuracy_residuals <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(
    fittedModel = accuracy_model
  )

  plot(accuracy_residuals)

} else {
  message(
    "Install DHARMa to perform simulation-based GLMM diagnostics."
  )
}
```

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# H2: RESPONSE TIME MODEL
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Residual diagnostics for the linear mixed model
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(
  fitted(rt_model),
  resid(rt_model),
  main = "RT Model: Residuals vs Fitted",
  xlab = "Fitted values",
  ylab = "Residuals"
)

abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

qqnorm(
  resid(rt_model),
  main = "RT Model: Normal Q-Q Plot"
)

qqline(resid(rt_model))

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

```

```{r}
)

# Save model summaries as text files

  summary(pas_model),
  file = "H1_PAS_model.txt"
)

capture.output(
  summary(accuracy_model),
  file = "H2_accuracy_model.txt"
)

capture.output(
  summary(rt_model),
  file = "H2_RT_model.txt"
)

cat("\nAnalysis completed.\n")
```
